newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO CETES RATE EASES DOWN ON PESO, LONG BOND.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO CETES RATE EASES DOWN ON PESO, LONG BOND.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 45 basis points to 18.75 percent in early trade on Tuesday due to a firm peso and lower yields on the U.S. long bond, dealers said.
"The peso has firmed against the dollar and long bond yields are down, so that has triggered some demand for local debt," a dealer said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were trading 2.65 centavos firmer at 7.7780/7.7805 per dollar in early dealing. The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was meanwhile up 17/32 to yield 6.60 percent.
Dealers said the market was cautious in the run-up to U.S. economic data later in the week and their possible impact on local financial markets through the U.S. long bond.
Overnight rates on bank paper had declined 95 basis points to yield 19.30 percent.
Liquidity of 144 million pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations. Dealers estimated a further 500 million pesos in cash would flow into the market.
